run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T02:31:19Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained at the proxy level: frontend-proxy's own spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR on its server span 'ingress' (increase 143.20 spans) and its client span 'router frontend egress' (94.45 spans) over the readable window, and its Envoy access log shows the corresponding 5xx responses. Two distinct mechanisms are visible. (1) A sharp burst of 500 via_upstream responses on only POST/GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, starting 02:33:53.371Z, 1.4 s after the old cart pod was told to stop (02:33:52Z) by a Deployment rollout (old ReplicaSet cart-755465879b scaled 1->0, new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d 0->1, cart container started 02:33:51Z, cart application startup line only at 02:34:14.911Z). The cart container has no readinessProbe and the Deployment runs 1 replica, so the serving replica was removed before the new application could listen. (2) A chronic, pre-existing pattern of 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} and a 504 UT response_timeout wave on /api/data (15000 ms), first visible at 02:11:32.659Z (request began ~02:11:17) and continuing to 02:40:54Z; this keeps the proxy error rate above 0 and explains why the alert starts 02:31:19Z, ~20 min after that onset (consistent with a for: clause, not verified). The frontend service is the upstream that returned the 500s/reset the connections: its own spans show ERROR increases on /api/cart, /api/checkout, gRPC CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect. The frontend pod never restarted, and its application logs could not be read, so the cause of the 503/504 component remains unresolved. fraud-detection OOMKilled (exit 137, restart 1) at 02:39:19Z is coincident and not tied to these errors.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR: over the readable window the ingress (server) span increased by 143.203125 error spans and the 'router frontend egress' (client) span by 94.453125, alongside 22299.876923 UNSET ingress spans.

Only two frontend-proxy span/status series pairs exist: span_name 'ingress' with span_kind SPAN_KIND_SERVER and span_name 'router frontend egress' with span_kind SPAN_KIND_CLIENT, each in STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

The 5-minute error rate of the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span was nonzero throughout the readable window, peaking at 0.3592592592592593 errors/s at the 02:36:19Z and 02:38:19Z samples and still 0.01274575/s at 02:48:19Z; the 'router frontend egress' error rate was nonzero only around 02:36-02:38 (0.34444444444444444/s).
At the last metric sample (02:48:19Z) the frontend-proxy ingress error rate was still 0.01274575/s and the egress rate 0, i.e. the proxy was still recording errors, not zero.

The frontend-proxy access log shows 57 5xx lines between 02:33:53.371559Z and 02:34:09.407688Z, all of them 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/cart' or 'POST /api/checkout' answered '500 - via_upstream' with 21-byte response bodies.

The proxy logged 100 5xx lines inside 02:30:00-02:40:00Z; besides the 500 via_upstream lines on /api/cart and /api/checkout (continuing to 02:34:21.213Z) it logged GET /api/products/* as '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' from 02:35:06.717Z to 02:38:25.894Z.

Earlier proxy 5xx: GET /api/data returned '504 UT response_timeout' with 15000/15001/15002 ms durations at 02:11:32.659Z-02:11:55.245Z, and 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} occurred on /api/products, /api/recommendations, /api/data and /api/cart between 02:12:21.488Z and 02:32:06.245Z.

After 02:39Z only one further 5xx was logged in the proxy log's readable range: GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4 '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' at 02:40:54.559247Z.

The frontend (the proxy's upstream) has its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases: POST /api/cart 52.83870967741935, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 52.852459016393446, GET /api/cart 23.370967741935484, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 23.37704918032787, POST /api/checkout 18.29032258064516, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.295081967213115, tcp.connect 7.114754098360656, 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 76.22950819672131 and '/api/checkout' 18.295081967213115, while /api/data and AdService/GetAds are 0.

The frontend's error rates peak in the same sampled minutes as the proxy's (02:36:19Z and 02:38:19Z): grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 0.1925925925925926/s, POST /api/cart 0.1925925925925926/s, POST 0.25925925925925924/s, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.06666666666666667/s, tcp.connect 0.02592592592592593/s.

Kubernetes events show a cart Deployment rollout: Deployment/cart 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' and ReplicaSet/cart-84889c965d SuccessfulCreate at 02:33:49Z, Pod/cart-84889c965d-tkxdz 'Started container cart' at 02:33:51Z, Pod/cart-755465879b-rh5r4 'Stopping container cart' and ReplicaSet/cart-755465879b SuccessfulDelete at 02:33:52Z, Deployment/cart 'Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0' at 02:33:52Z.

Pod objects: cart-84889c965d-tkxdz was created 02:33:49Z with container startedAt 02:33:51Z and restartCount 0, whereas every other demo pod was created 02:02:39Z-02:04:36Z; the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 was created 02:02:40Z, its container started 02:02:41Z and has restartCount 0.

The new cart container's log contains an ASP.NET startup line ('Overriding HTTP_PORTS ... Binding to values defined by URLS instead ...') at 02:34:14.911185Z; it was the only line in 02:30-02:40Z matching err/error/fail/exception/timeout/refused/unavailable/fatal out of 3382 lines read from that pod.

The cart Deployment runs replicas=1 with RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and its cart container has readinessProbe null (no readiness probe); frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog are also single-replica with readinessProbe null. Cart's container limits are cpu 45m / memory 165Mi, frontend's cpu 100m / memory 200Mi.

cart records no ERROR span status: its server spans POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, /GetCart and /EmptyCart and its client spans HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE and POST exist only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (plus a flagd EventStream ERROR series); checkout has client oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and server oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder series in both ERROR and UNSET.

The fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh restarted once with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-15T02:39:19Z, and its container startedAt 02:39:20Z; events show 'Created container: fraud-detection' and 'Started container fraud-detection' at 02:39:20Z. Its current log for 02:35-02:45Z contains Kafka 'Consumed record ... updated total count' lines and no line matching error/fail/exception.

The only traces Jaeger returned for frontend-proxy start at 02:19:43.871939Z-02:19:45.262283Z (data_as_of 02:19:45Z); in that 40-span slice every span has http.status_code 200 or 308 and none shows an error tag.

CPU CFS throttling ratios over the window: frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 0.36144116519739367, cart-84889c965d-tkxdz 0.5094408252153272, cart-755465879b-rh5r4 0.2761015023355637, product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-xcld7 0.20570757831413689, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt 0.09155851237866726, checkout-5dccddf8bb-cph2g 0; the frontend's ratio stayed between 0.31104356636271535 and 0.42994505494505497 across the 02:15-02:45Z samples.

Among span/HTTP/RPC metrics only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exist; no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series were returned. cAdvisor container_cpu_cfs_* and container_memory_* metrics do exist for the otel-demo containers.

The 500 via_upstream burst on /api/cart and /api/checkout (02:33:53.371Z-02:34:21Z) was caused by the cart Deployment rollout: the only cart pod was stopped at 02:33:52Z while the replacement's application had not started listening (its startup line appears only at 02:34:14.911Z), the frontend's cart and checkout handlers failed, and the frontend answered 500, which the proxy recorded as ingress/egress ERROR spans. Because the cart container has no readinessProbe, Kubernetes treats the new container as ready at start (02:33:51Z) and the old pod is removed about one second later.

The component that makes frontend-proxy's error rate nonzero before and after the cart burst is the intermittent frontend connection behaviour recorded as '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' plus the /api/data 15 s '504 UT response_timeout' wave. The earliest readable 5xx is the 02:11:32.659Z 504 whose 15000 ms duration implies a request start near 02:11:17Z; the alert's stated start at 02:31:19Z is about 20 minutes later, which is consistent with a 20-minute 'for' clause on an 'error rate above 0' condition (the rule itself was not readable).

The 503 UC responses are upstream-connection terminations raised by the frontend process during request handling (for example a keepalive/connection-close race with Envoy or a request aborted inside the Node.js frontend), not a frontend restart and not an error reported by a downstream service: frontend restarts are 0 and no downstream service shows an in-window error increase, but the frontend's own container logs could not be read, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.

The frontend's 100m CPU limit (36% of CFS periods throttled) may contribute to slow frontend responses such as the 15000 ms /api/data timeout, but throttling alone is not specific to this incident: cart-84889c965d-tkxdz was throttled 50.9% and product-catalog 20.6% over the same window.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 02:39:19Z) is not the cause of the frontend-proxy error burst: the main 500 wave ended at 02:34:21Z, the OOM restart at 02:39:20Z is followed by only one further logged 5xx (02:40:54.559Z), and fraud-detection's restarted container logged only normal Kafka consumption records.

A frontend pod crash/restart did not produce the 5xx: the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 was created at 02:02:40Z, its container started at 02:02:41Z and its restartCount is 0, so the 503 UC/500 responses came from a continuously running process.

The only trace slice available (02:19:43-02:19:45Z) shows frontend-proxy spans exclusively with http.status_code 200/308 and no error tags, so traces do not independently show the error requests; this slice covers about 1.2 s and therefore cannot rule out the metric- and log-derived error rate.

checkout shows no in-window error activity of its own: its oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder server and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart client ERROR series both increased by 0 over the window, so the frontend's failures on /api/checkout are not backed by a checkout error-rate reading.

The 503 UC/504 UT errors began around 02:11:32Z, roughly 22 minutes before the cart pod replacement (02:33:49-02:33:52Z), so the cart rollout cannot account for the whole nonzero error rate the alert reports.

Add a readinessProbe to the cart container (and the other single-replica demo Deployments with readinessProbe null) and use maxUnavailable 0 / more than one replica so a rolling update cannot stop the only serving cart pod while the new application is still starting.

To resolve the 503 UC/504 UT component, restore readability of the frontend container logs and compare the Envoy upstream keepalive/idle timeout settings with the frontend server's connection timeout, and check the frontend/cart CPU limits against observed throttling (36% and 51% of CFS periods).

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data both for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for an unfiltered listing, so its expression, evaluation window and 'for' duration are unverified; the reported threshold 'above 0 / current 0.01111111111111111' comes only from the untrusted Alertmanager payload.

The frontend application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 returned 0 lines / 0 bytes for 01:31:19-02:52:44Z, so the frontend's own reason for the 500 responses and the 503 UC connection terminations is unknown.

The previous (pre-restart) container logs of fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh and of the deleted cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 are not retrievable ('previous terminated container ... not found'), so what preceded the OOMKill and the cart shutdown sequence beyond one startup line is unknown.
Proxy access logs end at 02:44:32Z and span metrics at 02:48:19Z, so frontend-proxy behaviour between 02:44:32Z and 02:52:44Z (including whether 5xx continued) is unknown.

Jaeger retains only about 1-2 seconds of traces (spans at 02:19:43-02:19:45Z); traces_search and traces_search_by_tags (error=true, http.status_code="500") returned no matches in the error windows, so error traces for the 02:11-02:41Z events cannot be inspected.

No rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exist in this Prometheus, so gRPC status codes and HTTP status-code distributions cannot be verified from metrics.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so which change triggered the cart Deployment rollout at 02:33:49Z (and whether it was config-only, since the old pod's image digest is no longer observable) could not be determined.
Not all demo services were individually checked for their own error/latency signals (e.g. currency, payment, shipping, email, quote, kafka, valkey-cart); no claim is made about their state.

Whether the frontend-proxy latency or error level is abnormal relative to a longer baseline could not be established: span-metric data begins around 02:14Z, so no comparable pre-incident baseline exists in the readable window.
next_steps: Retrieve and read the frontend container's stdout/stderr (currently 0 bytes) and, if possible, the old cart pod's logs to confirm what the frontend reported when it returned 500 and when it reset upstream connections.

Inspect the frontend-proxy (Envoy) configuration for upstream keepalive/idle timeouts and route timeouts (the /api/data route timed out at 15000 ms) and compare with the frontend server's keep-alive settings.
Locate the RequestErrorRate rule in the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that owns it and confirm its expression, threshold and 'for' duration, then verify whether it kept firing after 02:48Z.
Review the change history of the cart Deployment around 02:33:49Z to identify the released change, since change_history is not integrated here.
Consider adding readiness probes and a second replica to cart (and the other single-replica demo deployments) and re-evaluate CPU limits for frontend and cart, given the observed throttling.
